The analysis considers a 5-MW composite wind turbine blade made of T300/QY8911 material.
The maximum internal stress in the composite blades is 718 MPa, and the ultimate stress is 1548 MPa.
The fatigue life cycles are calculated using a typical S-N curve model with parameters a = 1.816, b = 8.097, and m = 1.
The gamma process has three key properties: X(t)=0 at t=0, independent increments, and X(t)-X(s)~Ga(v(t-s),u) for t>s.
The probability density function of the fatigue damage D is given by the gamma distribution Ga(D|v,u).
The failure probability is calculated as the integral of the gamma probability density function from the critical damage level to infinity.
In the numerical example, the fatigue damage grows rapidly in the first 2 years, then increases slowly until around 20 years.
The failure probability reaches approximately 90% when the expected fatigue damage exceeds the given acceptable limit.
The manufacturing cost of the composite blades is about 15-20% of the total wind turbine production cost.
The typical design life for offshore wind turbines is 25-30 years.
The finite element model has three main components: the rotor, skin, and shear web.
The shear web helps resist the shear forces and improve the bending resistance of the composite blades.
The wind load is calculated using the wind pressure equation P = 0.5ρV^2Cp, where ρ = 1.29 kg/m^3 and Cp = 2.0.
The fatigue damage model parameters A and B are related by A = p + qB, where p = 1.816 and q = 0.44.
The gamma process can effectively model the gradual deterioration and uncertainties in the fatigue damage process.
